rubric.why: Kinematics is concerned with describing motion.
rubric.description: Identifies motion as the subject of kinematics.

rubric.why: Kinematics describes motion without explaining what causes it.
rubric.description: States that kinematics does not consider the causes of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that causes are not considered.

modelAnswer: Kinematics is the branch of physics that describes the motion of objects without considering the causes of that motion.

items.followUp: State the parallelogram rule for finding the resultant of two forces.

rubric.why: Successive force vectors are arranged by placing each new vector’s tail at the preceding vector’s head.
rubric.description: Describes arranging the force vectors head to tail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the correct head-to-tail arrangement.

rubric.why: The resultant joins the starting point of the vector chain to its final point.
rubric.description: States that the resultant goes from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both endpoints and the direction of the resultant.

modelAnswer: Draw the force vectors to scale, placing the tail of each new vector at the head of the previous one.
The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector, with its direction shown.
